title: shared_artefact_build_guard arm 6b enforces the 0285 scope property and cannot see a generated embed, so it passed on the lib/templates gap
body:
**`shared_artefact_build_guard.sh` arm 6b enforces exactly the property `0285`'s `lib/templates` limb violates. It ran on a commit at 2026-09-08 ~18:40Z and printed `ok`. It is structurally incapable of seeing that class, and so is the complement sweep that exists to catch what arm 6b misses.**

Filed separately from `0285` deliberately -- see the last section for why, because the same reasoning went the other way an hour earlier.

## What the arm claims

```
shared-artefact-guard: ok -- arm 6b -- every embed reaching outside its crate is covered
by the declared scope (3 embed(s) examined over 377 file(s) walked; both controls fired)
```

That is `0285`'s scope property, enforced per-commit, with working controls. **It passed while `lib/templates/{llm,prj}` reaches outside every declared scope and into the shipped binary.**

## Why it cannot see it -- two arms, two individually correct reasons

**Arm 6b's population is a grep for LITERAL `include_str!("...")` / `include_bytes!("...")` under `native/rust/crates`.** `build-support/embed_templates.rs` writes no literal: it WALKS a directory and GENERATES the embeds.

Driven at the artefact, 2026-09-08 19:0xZ:

```
native/rust/target/release/build/intentsvcs-54ac9798f099806d/out/embedded_templates.rs
  16 include_str! lines, eg
  include_str!("/Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intent/lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md")
  include_str!("/Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intent/lib/templates/llm/_ARCHETYPES.md")
```

**That path is outside `native/rust/crates`, so the population grep never reaches it.** And the complement sweep that exists to catch exactly this gap reads `native/rust` with `--exclude-dir=target` -- **correct for a build-output directory, and precisely where the generated embeds live.**

**So both arms are blind to the same class for two different and individually defensible reasons. A GENERATED embed is structurally invisible to a literal-grep census.** This is the A5 family at instrument level: not a control that failed, a control whose population cannot contain the subject.

## The guard is a good instrument and that is the point

**It NAMES its own boundary in its own output**, every run:

```
arm 6b NOT EXAMINED -- population is native/rust/crates (377 file(s) walked); the complement
sweep reads native/rust excluding target/ (383 file(s) walked) and found 1 embed(s) with a
`../` path outside the population, swept for and not examined.
```

It carries a vacuity control that fires, and `:261-305` records that it was already bitten once by an `include_str!` RESOLUTION bug and repaired. **This is the constructive form working as designed right up to its limit. The limit is the population, not the discipline** -- which is the same sentence as the other four findings of 2026-09-08, and the fourth time in one evening that a correct instrument answered about a population narrower than its claim.

**AND A GUARD THAT PRINTS ITS OWN BLIND SPOT ON EVERY RUN IS STILL READ AS A PASS.** The `NOT EXAMINED` line was in the output of the commit that shipped this gap, and in mine, and neither of us read it until the gap was found another way. A true signal nothing acts on is furniture -- which `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/measure.lib` already says in capitals about a different marker, and which nobody acted on there either.

## Not ruled, and no recommendation -- none of the three is priced

- **(a) Extend the population to `build-support/`.** Finds the WALK, not what it walks. Cheapest, weakest.
- **(b) Read the GENERATED files after a build.** The true artefact, and it couples a pre-commit guard to a build having happened -- which the guard's own arm 7 ordering was written to avoid.
- **(c) Declare build-script embeds a separate population with their own arm.** Most honest, most work.

## A location note, separate from the defect

The guard lives at `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/shared_artefact_build_guard.sh`. **A standing vc ruling already says that directory does not outlive `ST0056` and that this class of sweep belongs at `bin/.devbin/cmd/`.** Whoever takes this should not deepen an instrument in a home it is scheduled to leave.

## Why this is NOT a limb of `0285`, when the `lib/templates` finding WAS

**The same question was answered the other way an hour earlier and the discriminator is whether the remedies are one act.** `lib/templates` and the trigger gap are both `source_commit.rs`, both `DIRT_SCOPE`, one edit, one reader, one ruling -- so splitting them would have made two homes for one concern.

**This is a different file, a different instrument, three candidate remedies that share nothing with the `DIRT_SCOPE` change, and plausibly a different owner.** Fixing `DIRT_SCOPE` leaves this guard blind; fixing this guard leaves `DIRT_SCOPE` wrong. **Two concerns that reference each other are not one concern**, and folding them would bury an instrument defect inside a provenance row where nobody maintaining the guard would find it.

## Provenance

cc found it, verified it at the artefact level, and routed it rather than filing or fixing it. Re-driven here independently: the generated file, its 16 embeds, its location outside both populations, and the guard's own declaration of the boundary.


---

## CLOSED 2026-09-09 at `7f133373` (dc) -- ARM 6d, plus the scope gap it found

**The repair is a DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT rather than a fix to arm 6b, and that follows from this issue's own diagnosis.** A literal-`include_str!` census is structurally incapable of seeing a generated embed; making it see one would mean parsing Rust from shell, which the arm's own comments rule out as the coupling that fails in the dark. So arm 6b keeps its population and its declared boundary, and **arm 6d** takes the class it cannot reach.

**ARM 6d READS THE BUILD'S OUTPUT, NOT THE GENERATOR.** Reading the generator is inference, and the obvious parse -- every `.join("literal")` -- cannot tell an INPUT it walks from the OUTPUT file it writes, so it would red on `embedded_templates.rs` and refuse every commit in the repository for a path that is not a build input at all. The build output is measurement: it holds what the compiler was handed.

**ABSENCE IS REPORTED, NEVER SCORED AS ZERO.** A fresh checkout has no build output, so an arm that merely examined it would print a confident `ok` over a population of nothing -- this issue's own defect, reintroduced by its own fix. It prints NOT EXAMINED and names how many generators it could not read from.

**THE SCOPE GAP IS CLOSED TOO:** `lib/templates` joins `SHARED_TARGET_DIRT_SCOPES` on the grounds `docs/design` joined on 2026-08-30. Driven before landing -- `lib/templates` was clean, so the widening refused nobody's build. Arm 6 stays green because it requires guard-scope CONTAINS marker-scope and only the guard widened. **THE MARKER'S SCOPE STILL EXCLUDES `lib/templates`, AND THAT HALF IS `0285`, WHICH IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS.**

**TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING FROM THE BUILD, BOTH SELF-INFLICTED:**

- The first form reduced each embed to its ROOT before calling `embed_covered`, which asks whether a path is strictly INSIDE a scope -- so it compared `lib/templates` with itself, never matched, and red AFTER the scope was widened. **A green taken at that moment would have been read as the fix working.** Discrimination was therefore re-proven on the FIXED code with a real embed path (`lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md`): 3-entry scope UNCOVERED, 4-entry scope COVERED, control refused under both.
- The shell critic refused the first form as `IN-SH-CODE-001`, unquoted expansion, and it was right on this issue's own terms: a space in a build path turns one file into two that do not exist, `grep` opens neither, **and the arm reports a confident zero over a population it never read.** Rewritten with arrays; same 16 embeds, same verdict.

Verdict now: `arm 6d ok -- 16 embed(s) under 1 root(s), read from 10 generated file(s) written by 2 generator(s); both controls fired`.
